applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
New Zealand–United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement (effective 31 May 2023)
New Zealand–European Union Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 May 2024)
Double Tax Agreements with Australia, Singapore, the United States, and the United Kingdom

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993 (NZ), ss 21–24, 188–189; Companies (Registration) Regulations 1994; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, ss 5, 10–14, 17–23, 31, 46–58; Companies (Beneficial Ownership Disclosure) Amendment Act 2021; Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT Guidelines; United Nations Sanctions Regulations under the United Nations Act 1946; Russia Sanctions Act 2022; Terrorism Suppression Act 2002.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of each director and beneficial owner’s passport biometric page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the individual’s country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (HCCH 1961) in the state of issuance; Consular Legalization only for non-Hague issuers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incorporation (post-registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (MFAT)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership declaration and register of significant persons extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company itself (board resolution) and New Zealand Companies Office upon registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized company resolution; Hague Apostille by MFAT when required by foreign banks

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address (lease or utility bill)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized; Apostille by MFAT for overseas filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for intended B2B payment rails (Stripe Billing / Wise B2B)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The corporate or personal bank of the proposed directors/owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed bank letter authenticated by notary, Apostille only if demanded by payer bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and beneficial owners against: (i) NZ Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definition in AML/CFT Act 2009, s5; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) NZ autonomous sanctions regimes administered by MFAT, including the Russia Sanctions Act 2022; (iv) domestic Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 lists; and (v) supervised adverse-media and law-enforcement databases. Enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are compulsory for PEP or sanctions matches. OFAC screening is not a domestic statutory requirement but is required by Stripe Billing and Wise B2B for USD settlement and accepted best practice.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online registration and reserved-name portal (Companies Register) at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies/register/name-reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Latin script; te reo Māori macrons are accepted; Arabic numerals and limited punctuation (hyphen, apostrophe, bracket, ampersand, comma, full stop, slash, equals sign) are permitted; the name must not be identical or almost identical to any existing NZ company, overseas company, reserved name, or registered mark, and must not mislead as to the company’s nature or activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses a name, the applicant should file a written reconsideration request with the Companies Office Name Review section within 20 working days of the refusal notice, attaching supporting evidence. If refused again, the applicant may file an originating application for judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 challenging the Registrar’s exercise of statutory power; alternatively the applicant may simply reserve a new, non-conflicting name through the same portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only if the virtual office provider maintains a physical New Zealand street address that is open to the public for at least 30 hours per week, between 9 am and 5 pm on business days, as required by s188 Companies Act 1993. Pure mail-forwarding virtual addresses and PO Boxes do not satisfy the statute. For a B2B SaaS international company, a registered-office and corporate-agent service at a law-firm or licenced agent's premises is the recommended compliance structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate; assessed at approximately 15% during the first 12 months of operation, with regulator-driven address verification and possible unannounced site checks by the Companies Office, AML/CFT supervisor (FMA), or Inland Revenue where non-resident ownership or rapid revenue growth triggers enhanced review.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and name reservation (allocation and hold of proposed name)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation application, registration and certificate of incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed incorporation fee (currently NZD 115.70 inclusive of GST)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service, first year (physical address open to public)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office service provider / licensed corporate agent

AML/CFT compliance package (business risk assessment, compliance programme, UBO/PSC register, PEP and sanctions screening)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee benchmark for low-risk B2B SaaS incorporations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of KYC bundle (three directors/shareholders: passports, proof of address, UBO declarations)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff or prevailing local market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee (MFAT apostille: NZD 20 per document; consular fees vary)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12 to 16 (incorporation and constitution), sections 38 to 45 (issue of shares and capital), sections 189 to 194 (registered office and records), sections 201 to 206 (directors and resolutions); Companies (Forms) Regulations 1993; New Zealand Business Number Act 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), National Business Centre, Christchurch; online portal: companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, lodged through the Companies Office online company registration application; the filing also generates the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) and, if requested, IRD number allocation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a New Zealand company. The board may determine the issue price and consideration for shares under section 38 of the Companies Act 1993; no escrow account, capital deposit or undertaking is required at incorporation. A nominal issued capital of one New Zealand dollar per ordinary share is customary.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [INSERT COMPANY NAME] LIMITED. The initial subscribers’ board resolves as follows: 1. Share Capital Subscription: the subscription agreement between the company and the founding shareholder is approved. The board authorises the issue and allotment of [●] ordinary shares at NZD [●] per share, credited as fully paid at allotment. The amount subscribed shall be recorded in the share register and the shareholders’ ledger, and an initial capital statement in accordance with section 38 of the Companies Act 1993 shall be held at the registered office. 2. Registered Office: the registered office of the company is fixed at [●], New Zealand, and shall be open to the public for not less than ordinary business hours. The directors are authorised to file the corresponding notice with the Registrar of Companies and to adopt the registered office as the New Zealand address for service. 3. Appointment of Officers: [●] is appointed sole director and chair, and [●] is appointed company secretary, effective from the date of incorporation. Each officer accepts office subject to the company’s constitution and current legislation. 4. General Authority: any one director or the company secretary is authorised to execute all incorporation documents, open bank accounts, register with Inland Revenue and the Companies Office, and engage professional advisers to complete this formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, MBIE; online name reservation service via RealMe.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search through the Companies Office public register to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or almost identical to an existing registered name. Lodge the online name reservation application with the mandatory legal suffix 'Limited'. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee if applicable. A reserved name is held for 20 working days. No notarisation is required at this stage.
required_dossiers: RealMe identity verification of the applicant
Authority from the proposed subscriber to reserve the name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or queries the name, submit an alternative name through the same portal within the reservation window. If the rejection is due to a nearly-identical name, obtain a consent letter from the existing company or change the proposed name. A fresh name search and reservation fee may be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution, Director Consents and Subscriber Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office pre-filing review through the legal adviser or registered agent; final documents are lodged with the Registrar of Companies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the constitution (optional), director consents and subscriber information. If no constitution is adopted, the default provisions of the Companies Act 1993 will apply. Complete the consent to appointment for each director and the director particulars including full legal name, residential address, and date and place of birth. Confirm that at least one director is resident in New Zealand. Draft the share subscription agreement and state the number, class, issue price and consideration for the initial shares. The original signed documents must be retained by the company.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Director particulars and proof of identity
Share subscription agreement and capital schedule
Registered office and address for service details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar questions director residence, consent, or share consideration, obtain a corrective statutory declaration or board resolution and resubmit the amended documents through the Companies Office digital portal. Keep original signatures for seven years in accordance with record-keeping obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Lodgement and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE; companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office portal and select the application for incorporating a company. Enter the name reservation reference, company details, registered office, address for service, director and shareholder particulars. Attach the constitution, if any, and the consents to appointment. Verify each director’s identity through RealMe and the online consent step. Pay the statutory filing fee. The Registrar will issue the Certificate of Incorporation and, where requested, the NZBN and IRD number. Electronic authentication is accepted; no physical notarisation is required.
required_dossiers: Registered office and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond through the Companies Office portal within the specified period, ordinarily 20 working days, providing the missing statutory declarations or signed pages. If the Registrar declines incorporation, request a review of the decision and, if necessary, seek judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 for procedural unfairness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Statutory Records Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; local territorial authority for premises compliance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand, open to the public during ordinary business hours, and capable of receiving documents on behalf of the company. If the registered office was not already filed during incorporation, file the notice with the Companies Office. Maintain the company constitution, share register, director register, meeting minutes and financial records at the registered office. File any later change of registered office or address for service online.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and proof of authority to use the address
Notice of any change to director or shareholder particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a compliance notice relating to registered office or statutory records, remedy the default within ten working days and file the relevant corrective notice. Failure to comply may result in an infringement fee or court order; late changes can be filed with explanatory notes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, GST and Banking Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; Companies Office for IRD allocation on incorporation; banking institution for corporate account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If IRD registration was not completed at incorporation, apply for an IRD number through myIR. Register for GST if the value of taxable supplies exceeds NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period or if voluntary GST registration is desired to recover input credits. Register for PAYE and employer obligations when employees are engaged, and for RWT on dividends, interest and certain payments. Open a corporate bank account using the certificate of incorporation, constitution, NZBN confirmation and director identification. For B2B SaaS payment rails, complete merchant onboarding with Stripe and Wise using the bank account and corporate due diligence documents.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue raises a discrepancy, respond through myIR within 20 business days with the requested certificates and statutory declaration. If a bank or payment provider requests additional due diligence, provide the certified company extract from the Companies Office and an ultimate beneficial ownership schedule, and escalate to the provider’s compliance team if the response is delayed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ongoing Governance, Annual Returns and Payment Provider Onboarding Support
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office; Inland Revenue Department; merchant acquirers and regulated payment institutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, maintain the statutory registers at the registered office and file the annual return with the Companies Office each year. Notify the Registrar of any change of director, shareholder, registered office or address for service. Support the bank and payment service provider due diligence process by supplying the certificate of incorporation, NZBN certificate, beneficial ownership structure, source of funds information, and confirmation that the business is a B2B enterprise software service provider not requiring a sectoral licence. No financial markets or AML/CFT licence is triggered because the company does not provide regulated financial services; the payment service providers themselves remain subject to AML/CFT obligations.
required_dossiers: Certified certificate of incorporation and NZBN extract
Bank and payment provider due diligence forms
Annual return calendar and compliance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is overdue, file the overdue return promptly and pay the late filing penalty if any. If a bank or payment provider rejects the onboarding application, supply enhanced corporate ownership evidence and a business description referencing ISIC 6201 and NAICS 511210; if the rejection persists, apply to an alternative licensed payment service provider.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 enterprise software development. No New Zealand industrial licensing board or manufacturing licence is triggered because the company operates as a software publisher without physical production or industrial installation. If the company later leases a commercial office, the relevant territorial authority building consent authority applies under the Building Act 2004.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. A New Zealand enterprise SaaS company conducting cloud software development does not require an operating, manufacturing or sectoral licence. The governing requirement is the Certificate of Incorporation, plus ordinary business premises compliance and Inland Revenue registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable to a software-only activity; for any environmental regulatory matters the general regulators are the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and the relevant territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA-exempt. Software development and publishing are not listed activities under the Resource Management Act 1991; no full EIA report, environmental consent or registration is required for the core business. If a physical data centre is later leased, the data centre operator holds the relevant resource consents and building approvals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing emissions or waste streams are generated by the ordinary business. Any ancillary commercial office must comply with local authority wastewater trade-waste by-laws, the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for e-waste and office waste, and the Building Code ventilation requirement for indoor air quality. No VOC discharge limits apply to software code development.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No governmental occupational clearance is required for a low-risk office-based software company. The company must obtain a building warrant of fitness if the leased premises contain specified building systems, comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, and follow Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) guidance on fire evacuation arrangements. If structural alterations are made at the premises, building consent approval from the territorial authority is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Taake of New Zealand; online taxpayer portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident International Company (CK_IC): Step 1 - determine whether the entity has New Zealand-source income, a New Zealand taxable activity, or GST nexus under the remote-services rules; if none, no IRD/GST registration is required. Step 2 - obtain an IRD number by filing the IR 742 entity registration form (or online myIR 'Register a business/entity' application) together with the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, registered office details, director and ultimate beneficial owner information, and a non-resident declaration. IRD issues a 9-digit IRD number. Step 3 - if the entity carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, or supplies remote services to New Zealand consumers exceeding NZD 60,000 in 12 months, register for GST by filing the GST 1A application or the dedicated 'Remote services non-resident GST registration' in myIR. Step 4 - a foreign entity with no New Zealand fixed place of business may appoint a local agent or tax representative to manage IRD/myIR correspondence and return filing after registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (non-resident International Company without New Zealand central management and control or a permanent establishment; non-New Zealand-source income is outside the New Zealand income tax base; New Zealand-source income, if any, would be subject to entity-level taxation and non-resident withholding taxes as applicable)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not have a US-style 'check-the-box' election. Available statutory classification and tax elections include: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under the Income Tax Act 2007 for eligible close-held New Zealand companies, allowing owner-level taxation; (2) Foreign Investment Fund (FIF) method elections for interests in non-resident entities; (3) hybrid mismatch branch or deemed payment elections relevant where hybrid entities or instruments are present; (4) binding tax ruling applications under section 91C of the Tax Administration Act 1994 to confirm entity classification and GST treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added tax administered by the Inland Revenue Department under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (total taxable supplies in any 12-month period; the same threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of remote services supplied to New Zealand consumers under the GST remote-services rules, with voluntary registration available below the threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or electronic invoicing clearance by the tax authority. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates through the New Zealand Peppol e-invoicing framework. GST-registered businesses must issue tax invoices containing the statutory particulars prescribed by the GST Act 1985, and may retain digital records. No digital stamping or continuous transaction control mechanism is imposed; IRD uses myIR and post-event risk-based audit systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rating applies when goods are exported from New Zealand within 28 days of the time of supply and the supplier has obtained and retains satisfactory proof of export. Services: zero-rating may apply where services, including B2B enterprise SaaS, are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance and is not a New Zealand GST-registered person. Remote services supplied to New Zealand-resident non-GST-registered consumers are subject to 15% GST, not zero-rating. Supplies of remote services to GST-registered New Zealand businesses may be zero-rated where the recipient is a GST-registered person and the supply is acquired for the recipient's taxable activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic TSW/CUSDEC data accepted by New Zealand Customs Service)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (including Master Airwaybill where applicable)
Commercial invoice and underlying export contract or SaaS subscription agreement
Packing list and certificate of origin (where applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank foreign-exchange receipt evidencing payment and repatriation of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: IRD conducts targeted risk-based audits of zero-rated exports and may reclassify inadequately documented exports as standard-rated 15% GST supplies, requiring output tax plus use-of-money interest from the original refund date. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply: 20% for lack of reasonable care or unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or similar intent. Fraudulent export zero-rating claims can also expose the entity to criminal prosecution, fines up to NZD 250,000 per offence for a company, and imprisonment for responsible persons. Documentary proof of physical export for goods and actual supply to an eligible non-resident recipient for services is mandatory and must be retained to support refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua (the central bank and prudential regulator for registered banks, non-bank deposit takers, and insurers under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989; foreign investment screening is administered separately by the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) under the Overseas Investment Act 2005; AML/CFT supervision of banks is co-led by the Reserve Bank, the Financial Markets Authority (FMA), and the Department of Internal Affairs under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully and freely convertible. New Zealand maintains no exchange controls, no foreign currency rationing, and no government licensing requirement for current-account or capital-account transactions. Capital-account restrictions are limited to OIO screening for sensitive land and significant business assets (e.g., 25%+ shareholdings or high-value infrastructure), which do not apply to a pure ISIC 6201 cloud software licensing vehicle that holds no land, media, or sensitive quota. Profit and dividend remittance from an NZ-incorporated International Company is legally unrestricted; the only frictions are tax-related: non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) applies to dividends (30% statutory, reduced by double-tax treaties, e.g., 15% to Australia/UK/Germany, 0% in limited fully-imputed scenarios) and royalty outflows are subject to NRWT at 15% (5% under the NZ–US treaty for qualifying software royalties). The entity may hold and operate multi-currency accounts in NZD, USD, EUR, and major APAC currencies; no prior central bank approval is required for conversion at any quantum.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation time-window exists in New Zealand. The Reserve Bank’s balance-of-payments statistical framework (Banking System Monthly Statistics and Standard Credit Reporting) requires licensed banks to categorise cross-border receipts by BPM6 purpose codes, but the underlying SaaS/software-licence revenue (export of cloud services) may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely, netted, or converted into NZD at the exporter’s commercial discretion. For an ISIC 6201 enterprise SaaS supplier, subscription receipts should be coded under EBOPS code 9.2 / services purpose code S42, and there is no obligation to surrender export proceeds to an authorised dealer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency NZD/USD/EUR/GBP) and segregated Capital Escrow Account for investor subscriptions

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of New Zealand (BNZ) — National Australia Bank subsidiary
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account with NZClear/ESAS participation; commercial letters of credit incorporated

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: ASB Bank Limited (Commonwealth Bank of Australia group)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with modern API connectivity for Stripe/Wise treasury flows; inwards/outwards SWIFT
Operational Account plus committed FX forward lines; Capital Escrow Account available

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH for thin-rail treasury operations (collections and vendor disbursements), but MEDIUM-LOW as a replacement for a licensed bank for escrow/holding of statutory capital. Wise Business (NZ) is registered on the FMA’s Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) and is supervised for AML/CFT by the FMA; it cannot take deposits or lend, but can hold safeguarded funds and process cross-border SaaS subscription receipts in over 50 currencies. Stripe Billing/Balance is a payment facilitator under Visa/Mastercard rules rather than a licensed NZ bank, settling payouts via an NZ acquiring bank. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs are not authorised to hold statutory share-capital escrow for an NZ IC, so capital injection must route to a licensed commercial bank; (ii) FX hedging contracts cannot be executed with an unlicensed EMI; and (iii) bank references from EMIs are not accepted by NZClear. The blueprint therefore adopts a hybrid 'Wise + Stripe for commerce rails, Tier-1 bank for fiduciary and hedge rails' architecture.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Electronic Identity Verification Amendment Act 2020, remote video verification and digital ID are permissible for low-risk corporate clients. Physical presence of all directors and UBOs is NOT a hard statutory mandate; however, each Tier-1 bank retains discretion and, in practice, requires: (i) a physical or video meeting with at least one director or a senior officer controlling the account; (ii) the company’s NZ registered office and a local contact agent (lawyer/accountant of FMA-regulated status); and (iii) for UBOs residing in offshore trust jurisdictions, full trust deeds and a trust-registry certificate. A director is not normally required to travel to Auckland/Wellington when opening through a corporate advisory desk with a complete KYB package; the stated service-level objective is 7–10 business days for fully remote onboarding of a low-risk ISIC 6201 entity, versus 3–5 days with a branch visit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or company appears in a jurisdiction flagged by the bank’s compliance engine as a tax haven or FATF grey-listed territory (e.g., Cook Islands flag despite associated-state status).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion from an NZ-qualified lawyer confirming good standing and lawful incorporation; FATCA/CRS attestation and tax-residence certificates of ultimate shareholders; source-of-capital and source-of-wealth report from a Big-4 firm; two years of audited financial statements or a business plan with pro-forma balance sheet; board resolution appointing the NZ director and authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction flows routing through high-risk corridors (crypto exchanges, OFAC/UN-sanctioned jurisdictions, or substantial receivables from shell entities).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction flowchart per payment rail (payer → Stripe/Wise → bank); sanctions-screening report from the bank’s own monitoring system; executable SaaS terms of service evidencing bona fide cloud-software licensing; undertaking to provide quarterly KYC refreshes and a named Data Protection Officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trust- or partnership-owned IC where discretionary beneficiaries obscure the natural-person controlling the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed with all amendments; trustee resolution appointing an independent NZ director; register of significant controllers (RSIC) filed under the Companies Act 1993; legal opinion confirming trust validity and that effective management and control rests with identifiable parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionately large nominal capital injection (e.g., above NZD 2M) for an early-stage SaaS company, or frequent intercompany flows with non-resident subsidiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valuation report on the cloud-software platform; share subscription agreements referencing the ISIC 6201 purpose; transfer-pricing memorandum documenting arm’s-length intercompany SaaS royalties and cost-plus markups; 18-month funds-flow forecast evidencing deployment of escrowed capital for R&D and cloud hosting rather than passive wealth storage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the NZ-incorporated IC, inbound equity capital is routed via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or MT202 (bank-to-bank) into a Tier-1 bank-designated Capital Escrow Account. The payment instruction must carry the RBNZ/BPM6 financial-account code F1.1.1 (equity) or the bank’s equivalent 'non-resident equity inward' purpose code; the reference field must state: 'INJECTION OF SHARE CAPITAL, [Company Name], ISIC 6201, pursuant to board resolution [date], subscriber [name], share class/quantity'. A cover letter attaching the shareholder registry, board minutes, and executed subscription agreement is retained by the beneficiary bank. No OIO consent is required because the entity owns no sensitive assets; only standard balance-of-payments statistical capture with monthly RBNZ reporting applies. The bank verifies the ultimate transferor under FATF Recommendation 16; funds arriving from a trust bank account must present the same UBO chain.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and cloud-R&D disbursements use SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) with services purpose codes (S42 for software/cloud, S61 for R&D) and MT202 for correspondent refinancing. Dividend and royalty outflows to shareholders use MT103 with a tax indicator; NRWT is withheld electronically and paid to Inland Revenue under the applicable DTA rate. Commercial letters of credit (Sight L/C and Usance L/C under ICC UCP 600) are available for any physical-goods components, though for a pure SaaS company they are used only where a global reseller contract requires them. All NZD legs settle via NZClear’s ESAS (Exchange Settlement Account System) operated by the Reserve Bank; foreign-currency legs settle via the bank’s correspondent network. The target payment rails operate as: Stripe Billing → merchant acquiring → settlement in NZD to the company’s ANZ/BNZ account; Wise B2B → multi-currency wallet → FX conversion to USD/EUR → treasury or vendor payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (outright and swap) in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD, and NZD/GBP under an ISDA/CSA master agreement with a licensed NZ bank
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for hedging the notional of intercompany IP-financing or capital-structure loans
European-style FX options (premium-paid) for committed M&A or multi-year contract exposure requiring insurance against adverse NZD moves
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) as a backstop only where an offshore counterparty cannot accept physical delivery of NZD
Interest-rate swaps and commodity derivatives incidental to treasury risk management, with no speculative trading permitted under board policy
All hedging instruments must be executed with an FMA-licensed or qualifying derivative issuer under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with the company qualifying as an eligible investor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (confirmation of registered particulars, directors, shareholders, and beneficial ownership) together with annual government renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Services Development Authority (FSDA), Government of the Cook Islands (Realm of New Zealand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of incorporation; recurring annually, with the filing window closing on the anniversary date specified by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues at the prescribed rate; if the annual fee remains unpaid for 3 months after written notice from the Registrar, the company may be struck off from the International Companies Register, automatically losing good standing and tax-exempt status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under the International Companies Act for a standard international company; no statutory audit is required. Compulsory audit may arise only if the company is separately licensed as an international bank, insurance, or trust business, or if required by an investor, lender, or parent-company undertaking.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory financial-statement filing framework; accounting records may be maintained under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or IFRS for SMEs on a voluntary basis, but no financial statements are filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must verify the identity and shareholding of all members and beneficial owners annually as at the anniversary date. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Register of Members and the Beneficial Ownership Register at the registered office; the agent files a notice of any change in beneficial ownership with the Registrar within 14 days, and the annual return confirms that all share transfers during the year have been recorded and all current beneficial owners are correctly identified. The UBO register is confidential and not open to public inspection.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 1,500 per annum including registered agent, registered office, and corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; voluntary audit preparation typically USD 4,000 - 10,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a compliant Cook Islands International Company (statutory exemption under the International Companies Act 2011-12, Cook Islands); 28% for the New Zealand corporate rate if the IC is trapped into New Zealand tax residence by central management and control being exercised in New Zealand
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory total exemption for the IC from Cook Islands income tax, capital gains tax, dividend/interest/royalty withholding taxes, and value-added or goods-and-services taxation; New Zealand applies a 0% effective rate to the IC as a non-resident company to the extent it derives no New Zealand-source income; the schema default loss-carryforward figure of 5 years is non-jurisdictional for this structure because the exempt IC cariies a nil taxable base; if New Zealand residence were triggered as a red flag, New Zealand tax losses carry forward indefinitely, subject to a 49% shareholder continuity test, and are not absorbed by this structure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cook Islands International Company Annual Return (Registrar of International Companies, Financial Supervisory Commission portal, submitted exclusively through the licensed registered agent)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within one calendar month following each anniversary of incorporation; the filing window is the anniversary date plus 30 days, subject to a Registrar-issued alternative return date by notice

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal Name of the International Company as registered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact registered name; a foreign-language or abbreviated trading name attached to the B2B SaaS contracting entity must be cross-referenced to the registered number-plate or corporate name

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Office Address in the Cook Islands
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the full street address of the licensed registered agent; a post-office box alone is non-compliant, and the address must be in Rarotonga or another approved Cook Islands locality

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed Registered Agent and Fiduciary Details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the licensed trustee or corporate services provider; the registered agent is the regulatory entry point for AML and ESR filings and must remain independent of the NZ-resident beneficial owner

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors: Full Names, Nationalities, and Residential Addresses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all directors and the country of tax residence for each; any director resident in New Zealand creates a rebuttable inference of NZ central management and control and triggers the NZ 28% residence trap

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Shareholders and Beneficial Ownership Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify all registered shareholders and the ultimate beneficial owner; the beneficial owner declaration must be consistent with the AML/CFT customer due diligence file retained by the registered agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued Share Capital and Share Classes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the authorised and issued share capital, including no-par-value shares and any preferred/management classes used for the enterprise SaaS cap table
Declare solvency and confirm that no winding-up order, receivership, or tax charge is outstanding against the IC

Indicate whether the IC carries on a relevant activity; for a B2B SaaS IP-holder, confirm local decision-making, local employees, premises, and operating expenditure commensurate with the software licence income, or declare a pure equity holding position if no active trade exists

State the jurisdiction where strategic commercial decisions, board meetings, and financial control are actually exercised; answering New Zealand converts the IC to an NZ-resident taxpayer and triggers the IR4 filing obligation and CFC disclosure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Cook Islands IC annual return attracts a statutory late-filing monetary penalty per month of default, suspension from transacting business, automatic deregistration at the Registrar's discretion, and a mandatory breach report by the registered agent to the Financial Supervisory Commission; directors remain personally responsible for all unperformed filings and penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: New Zealand IR4 Annual Income Tax Return (Inland Revenue, myIR secure electronic filing system)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due on 7 July immediately following the balance date; for a non-standard balance date, the return is due no later than the last day of the sixth month after the balance date; provisional tax instalments apply quarterly to an NZ-resident company

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Reconciliation and Total Assessable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC deriving no New Zealand-source income, enter nil and attach a schedule of foreign-sourced SaaS subscription revenue; any NZ-source income arising from cloud services performed through an NZ fixed base must be disclosed in full
Allow only New Zealand-source deductions; cross-border allocations to offshore R&D, marketing, or shared services are non-deductible in the absence of contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation
Compute taxable income at 28%; losses from the exempt Cook Islands IC cannot be offset against NZ income of connected persons; loss utilisation requires a shareholder continuity schedule
Declare any New Zealand-sourced dividends, interest, or royalties derived by the IC and the DTA-reduced NRWT rate claimed; attach the Cook Islands Tax Residency Certificate and the IR290 declaration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Director Signature and Declaration of Truthfulness
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by a director with actual knowledge of the affairs; a knowingly false declaration is an evasion offence and triggers personal liability for shortfall penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the NZ IR4 incurs a NZ$250 initial penalty plus NZ$50 per month for each month of default, use-of-money interest at the current prescribed rate on any unpaid tax, and shortfall penalties on the tax ultimately assessed; deliberate non-filing escalates to penalties of up to 150% of the avoided tax and criminal prosecution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for a Cook Islands International Company because the IC is statutorily excluded from all Cook Islands withholding taxes; under the New Zealand-Cook Islands DTA, NZ NRWT on a dividend paid to a New Zealand-resident beneficial owner is capped at 15% generally and 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 10% of the voting power; New Zealand domestic NRWT on dividends is 30% for non-imputed dividends and 15% for fully imputed dividends, but no NZ NRWT arises on a true IC dividend that is sourced outside New Zealand
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must: (1) obtain a Cook Islands Tax Residency Certificate from the Cook Islands Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; (2) complete the New Zealand IR290 'Residency and Withholding Tax Declaration' or the equivalent NRWT reduced-rate application; (3) deliver the TRC and declaration to the New Zealand withholding agent or Inland Revenue before the payment date so that the reduced treaty rate is applied at source; (4) where over-withholding has occurred, file a refund claim with the competent authority of the source country within the statutory time-bar; reciprocal exchange of information under the DTA confirms treaty residence and supports the reduced rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Cook Islands IC: 0% statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest; New Zealand domestic NRWT: 15% on cross-border interest and 15% on royalties, with a 0% rate available on interest paid by an Approved Issuer under the Approved Issuer Levy regime; New Zealand-Cook Islands DTA: maximum source-state withholding of 10% on interest and 10% on royalties, subject to genuine beneficial ownership and absence of treaty shopping

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand thresholds in NZD: mandatory Local File when cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$10 million annually; mandatory Master File when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds NZ$50 million and related-party cross-border transactions exceed NZ$10 million; Country-by-Country Report when group consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750 million (approximately NZ$1.3 billion); the Cook Islands maintains OECD-aligned transfer pricing rules under the Income Tax Act 1997 with no published statutory monetary de minimis for International Companies, so all intercompany SaaS licence fees, R&D cost contributions, distribution margins, and financing arrangements must be substantiated under the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cook Islands applies Economic Substance Requirements under the International Companies Act 2011-12 and the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations, implementing the OECD/G-20 harmful tax practices framework; relevant activities, including IP holding, distribution and service centres, financing, and pure equity holding, require: (1) economic substance directed and managed in the Cook Islands; (2) adequate local premises, employees, and annual operating expenditure proportionate to the income; and (3) an annual economic substance filing; a B2B enterprise SaaS IP-holder is classified as a high-risk IP company that must demonstrate active decision-making by local directors, substantive local staffing for operational functions, and no bare passive holding of intangibles; failure to satisfy ESR is automatically exchangeable with New Zealand under the OECD exchange-of-information framework

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / New Zealand Residence Trapping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Central management and control of the Cook Islands IC is exercised from New Zealand, such as NZ-resident directors convening board meetings in Auckland, New Zealand-based strategic decision-making, or operational IT management located in New Zealand, causing the IC to become an NZ tax resident while it fails to file an NZ IR4, fails to disclose its CFC position, and pays no New Zealand income tax on worldwide SaaS revenues
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: New Zealand corporate income tax at 28% on worldwide income; shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 of 20% for gross carelessness, 40% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion; criminal conviction for knowingly evading tax carries a fine of up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years, together with use-of-money interest, asset restraint orders, and seizure of the SaaS revenue stream
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where NZ management-and-control facts are attributable to directors; directors may be jointly and severally liable for shortfall penalties, unpaid PAYE and GST obligations attach to directors personally, and criminal sanctions extend to disqualification from holding office as a director of any New Zealand or Cook Islands company, departure prohibition orders and travel bans, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC operates as a bare licence-registry shell for the enterprise SaaS intellectual property with no physical office in the Cook Islands, nominee directors lacking substantive authority, no local payroll, no board minutes evidencing real commercial decisions, and non-arm's-length royalty payments routed to connected persons; this is a high-risk IP company profile under ESR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cook Islands ESR regime: prohibition on transacting business, monetary penalties of up to CI$250,000 for non-compliance, deregistration by the Registrar, and mandatory automatic exchange of information with New Zealand under the Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters; where New Zealand taxing rights exist, the arrangement is recharacterised as a sham, with reassessment at 28% and evasion penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are personally liable for ESR penalties when the company defaults on payment; courts may disqualify directors for up to 5 years, impose personal travel bans pending investigation, and order personal restitution to shareholders where the shell structure was used to conceal asset misappropriation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or file the register of beneficial owners, use of bearer arrangements or nominee-trustee layers to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner of the B2B SaaS entity, or processing high-volume subscription payments through Stripe Billing and Wise B2B without conducting customer due diligence on sources of funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Cook Islands AML/CFT Act civil fines of up to CI$300,000 per contravention for non-filing and for failure to perform customer due diligence; deliberate money laundering under the Cook Islands Proceeds of Crime Act and the New Zealand Crimes Act carries imprisonment of up to 7 years, freezing and forfeiture of SaaS subscription revenue, and disqualification orders against corporate service providers; suspicious transactions must be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly or recklessly permits money laundering through the IC is personally indictable for aiding and abetting; personal asset forfeiture, travel bans, and extradition exposure can be imposed; the corporate veil is pierced where the director directed the non-compliant conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC books enterprise software licensing revenue through arrangements that are not at arm's length, including economically unsupported royalty rates, cost-plus margins compressed below OECD minimum levels, payments for shareholder services disguised as technical fees, or circular intercompany financing without market-based interest rates
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: New Zealand Inland Revenue may recharacterise and adjust the royalty, service fee, or interest base, assess additional income tax at 28%, and impose transfer pricing adjustment penalties under sections FB 2 to FB 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007; shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% of the adjusted tax apply, and non-production of contemporaneous documentation reverses the burden of proof
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or direct non-arm's-length intercompany agreements can be jointly assessed for civil penalties; egregious deliberate mispricing elevates the conduct to criminal evasion with personal criminal liability; where the company is insolvent at the assessment date, directors face personal liability for the company's shortfall and reimbursement orders
